title: Five topics that win an Enterprise AI Architect offer
oneliner: Be able to explain, end to end: a multi-agent implementation, AI governance, model observability, the MLOps pipeline, and your prompt-engineering approach.
says: To secure an enterprise AI architect offer, nail five topics: how you would implement a multi-agent system for a concrete use case (his example: a customer-support organization); how you implement AI governance in your AI project; how you implement model observability for an agent project; how you build the MLOps pipeline end to end; and how you approach prompt engineering.
explained: Read the five as one system, not five subjects. Multi-agent design is the architecture; governance is what makes it deployable in an enterprise; observability is how you operate it; MLOps is how you ship changes safely; prompt engineering is the interface layer where behavior is actually controlled. A candidate who connects them - 'the pipeline deploys prompt versions, observability catches the regressions, governance defines what may ship' - sounds like someone who has run a real system.

Note the demand for concreteness: 'for a particular use case.' Interviewers are filtering out slideware. Pick one use case you know well - customer support is his example because it is the industry's default - and be able to walk these five layers on it without notes.
takeaway: One use case, five layers: multi-agent design, governance, observability, MLOps, prompting. Rehearse them as one connected system.
